_comment: RAM addresses whose names are supported by evidence. Key: hex address. Each entry: name, note (what the evidence shows), evidence (id in docs/EVIDENCE_LOG.md). Addresses not listed get address names (wXXXX, hXXXX, sXXXX) with no meaning claimed.

C525.name: wIsCGB
C525.note: 1 when the boot code found A = $11 (CGB), else 0; set at $0150

D7FE.name: wDataBank
D7FE.note: ROM bank used by Func_000_0B6C when reading a word through HL

D067.name: wDataBankSave
D067.note: spare slot some code copies wDataBank to and restores it from

DD10.name: wSoundId
DD10.note: sound id passed to the start-sound routine

DC00.name: wSoundChannelSlots
DC00.note: channel-state slots; the record's first byte is added to this address

DCC0.name: wSoundLabelSlots
DCC0.note: per-channel label slots: 3 bytes each, 16 per channel

DD0F.name: wSoundChannelIndex
DD0F.note: slot number of the channel the sound engine is processing

DD0A.name: wSoundHwChannel
DD0A.note: hardware channel of the current slot: 2 selects the wave channel, 3 noise

FFDD.name: hSoundBank
FFDD.note: ROM bank the sound engine reads tracks from

FFD8.name: hTrackPosLo
FFD8.note: low byte of the current track position, counted in 2-byte events

FFD9.name: hTrackPosHi
FFD9.note: high byte of the current track position

FFDB.name: hTrackBaseLo
FFDB.note: low byte of the current track's start address

FFDC.name: hTrackBaseHi
FFDC.note: high byte of the current track's start address

FFD6.name: hDecompressLock
FFD6.note: non-zero while the decompressor is running

FFBB.name: hDecompressMarker
FFBB.note: marker byte from the stream header

FFA1.name: hScrollX
FFA1.note: copied to rSCX by Func_000_07E0 and by the LCD handler

FFA5.name: hScrollY
FFA5.note: copied to rSCY by Func_000_07E0 and by the LCD handler

FFB1.name: hOamNextEntry
FFB1.note: index of the next 4-byte entry BuildOamFromSpriteTable writes at $C000; it stops at $28

C0A2.name: wMenuRowCount
C0A2.note: number of cursor rows UpdateMenuCursor wraps over (E-0060)

C0A3.name: wMenuPageCount
C0A3.note: number of pages UpdateMenuCursor steps through with Left/Right; 0 or 1 disables paging (E-0060)

C0A5.name: wMenuLastPageRows
C0A5.note: rows on the last page; UpdateMenuCursor clamps the row to this minus 1 there (E-0060)

C0A6.name: wMenuPage
C0A6.note: current page index set by UpdateMenuCursor (E-0060)

C53D.name: wStringDestLo
C53D.note: low byte of the destination CopyStringToBuffer writes the string to (E-0059)

C53E.name: wStringDestHi
C53E.note: high byte of the destination CopyStringToBuffer writes the string to (E-0059)

C528.name: wStringCategory
C528.note: category index LookupString uses in the table of tables

C529.name: wStringIndex
C529.note: index within the category table that LookupString uses

C52A.name: wStringBank
C52A.note: ROM bank number LookupString stores; the string printer maps it into the ROM bank window

FFA9.name: hSpriteOriginX
FFA9.note: added to each entry's X (+8) by BuildOamFromSpriteTable

FFAB.name: hSpriteOriginY
FFAB.note: added to each entry's Y (+$10) by BuildOamFromSpriteTable

FFAD.name: hSpriteSetIndex
FFAD.note: first-level index into the table BuildOamFromSpriteTable reads

FFAE.name: hSpriteSubIndex
FFAE.note: second-level index into the table BuildOamFromSpriteTable reads

FFAF.name: hSpriteTileOffset
FFAF.note: added to each entry's tile number by BuildOamFromSpriteTable

FFB0.name: hSpriteAttrXor
FFB0.note: XORed into each entry's attribute byte by BuildOamFromSpriteTable

CB7F.name: wSpriteSlots
CB7F.note: start of an array of objects: 8-byte slots in the bank $E0 intro (DrawSpriteSlots), 16-byte entries in field mode (the script commands, ScriptStepObject)

C198.name: wScreenTileBuffer
C198.note: screen tile buffer: the $240 bytes are cleared with $C3; CopyTileBufferToBGMap and CopyBlockToTileBuffer use rows of 32 bytes, while field mode (Func_002_59CD) indexes it with rows of 20 and 260 of its 360 visible entries equal the BG map on the emulator (E-0030)

C524.name: wSGBActive
C524.note: set to 1 at boot, cleared on CGB and when DetectSGB finds no Super Game Boy; SendSGBPacketSet, DelayBCWhenSGB and SpinDelay return at once when it is 0

C47C.name: wSGBPacketIndex
C47C.note: packet set number for SendSGBPacketSet; $FF selects wSGBPacketBuffer

C47F.name: wSGBPacketBuffer
C47F.note: packet data used by SendSGBPacketSet when wSGBPacketIndex is $FF

C5DB.name: wGameMode
C5DB.note: index into the 9-entry tables RunGameModeInit and RunGameModeUpdate use; 5 at boot

C5DF.name: wModeChangeRequest
C5DF.note: non-zero makes the main loop leave its wait and run RunGameModeInit again

C56C.name: wFadeState
C56C.note: palette fade state set by StartPaletteFade; GameFrameUpdate and the VBlank handler skip normal work while it is non-zero (bit 7 clear)

C55E.name: wJoypadHeld
C55E.note: buttons held at the latest PollJoypad (layout of ReadJoypadDirect)

C562.name: wJoypadPressed
C562.note: buttons newly held since the previous poll

C564.name: wJoypadRepeatTimer
C564.note: auto-repeat countdown: $14 after a new press, then 6

C5F0.name: wFrameCounterLo
C5F0.note: low byte of the 16-bit frame counter the VBlank handler increments

C5F1.name: wFrameCounterHi
C5F1.note: high byte of the 16-bit frame counter

C60A.name: wMusicRequest
C60A.note: music id waiting for ProcessSoundQueue; $FF = none

C60B.name: wSoundEffectRequest
C60B.note: sound effect id waiting for ProcessSoundQueue; $FF = none

C5DC.name: wModeState
C5DC.note: per-mode sub-state; low nibble indexes the jump table in GameMode1_Update (E-0030)

FFA2.name: hScrollXHi
FFA2.note: high byte of the 16-bit horizontal scroll that starts at hScrollX

FFA6.name: hScrollYHi
FFA6.note: high byte of the 16-bit vertical scroll that starts at hScrollY

FFAA.name: hSpriteOriginXHi
FFAA.note: high byte of the 16-bit sprite X position (hSpriteOriginX is the low byte)

FFAC.name: hSpriteOriginYHi
FFAC.note: high byte of the 16-bit sprite Y position (hSpriteOriginY is the low byte)

FFD2.name: hSpriteScrollXLo
FFD2.note: low byte of -(scroll X - 9) - 1, computed each frame by ComputeSpriteScrollOffsets

FF98.name: hPlayerFacing
FF98.note: 0, 1, 2, 3: CheckInteractionInFront adds +16 to hFF91, +16 to hFF8E, -16 to hFF91, -16 to hFF8E for these values

FF8E.name: hPlayerX
FF8E.note: position along the axis that facings 1 and 3 change in CheckInteractionInFront

FF91.name: hPlayerY
FF91.note: position along the axis that facings 0 and 2 change in CheckInteractionInFront

C82D.name: wPlayFrames
C82D.note: frame count 0-59 of the play-time counter

C830.name: wPlayHoursLo
C830.note: low byte of the 16-bit play-time hours

C831.name: wPlayHoursHi
C831.note: high byte of the 16-bit play-time hours

D968.name: wSlotPersonalityHi
D968.note: first of three byte arrays (8 slots each) graded into the personality index with weight 9 by PersonalityIndexOfSlot

D2C7.name: wPersonalityIndex
D2C7.note: column index (0-26) into the bank-6 table; set from PersonalityIndexOfSlot in banks $30 and $E0 before ReadBank6TableWord

CFEC.name: wRecordBuffer
CFEC.note: scratch buffer shared by the record loaders: LoadSkillRecord reads its first word as the skill number and writes 17 bytes after it; LoadMonsterRecord stores a 26-byte monster record here

CFEE.name: wRecordBufferData
CFEE.note: where LoadSkillRecord puts the 17 bytes of a skill record (byte 2 of the buffer)

CFE6.name: wMonsterId
CFE6.note: 16-bit monster id (wCFE7 is the high byte) that LoadMonsterRecord reads

D081.name: wItemId
D081.note: item id used by LoadItemRecord and RunItemEffect; $FF = none

C61D.name: wInventory
C61D.note: 24-slot bag of item ids (searched by FindTemp0InInventoryList; empty at the start of a new game)

FF90.name: hMapId
FF90.note: map number: indexes MapTable (bank $11); 29 on the opening ship deck; the map's name is the system string at index 10 + number ('Deck' for 29, 'NO' for the unused 30, 31, 39)

FF8F.name: hMapScreenX
FF8F.note: column of the current screen in the map: LoadMapScreen indexes the map's array of screen streams with hMapScreenY * width + hMapScreenX (1 on the opening ship deck, a map 2 screens wide)

FF92.name: hMapScreenY
FF92.note: row of the current screen in the map (0 on the opening ship deck)

C190.name: wMapWidthScreens
C190.note: map width in screens, from the map record (2 for the ship deck, 4 for map 56)

C191.name: wMapHeightScreens
C191.note: map height in screens, from the map record

C192.name: wMaxBlockingTile
C192.note: highest tile id that blocks the player (TileBlockedAtPixel compares tile ids with it); from the map record (55 for the ship deck)

C919.name: wScriptStartRequest
C919.note: bit 7 set asks FetchScriptCommand to begin running the script at wScriptPointer

C91A.name: wScriptPointerLo
C91A.note: low byte of the address of the next script byte (wC91B is the high byte; the bytes are in the current bank, or in wDataBank when wScriptInDataBank is set)

C91B.name: wScriptPointerHi
C91B.note: high byte of the script pointer

C7CC.name: wSpeciesFlags
C7CC.note: one bit per monster id (bit id & 7 of byte id / 8; TestSpeciesFlag, SetSpeciesFlag); counted per family by CountSpeciesPerFamilyFlaggedOrListed. What the bit records (for example a library entry) is not checked (E-0070)

C617.name: wGoldLo
C617.note: low byte of the 24-bit gold amount: the new-game setup sets 100 (InitGoldAndClearInventory), AddGoldCapped caps it at 99,999 and DrawGoldPanel_Bank24 shows it in decimal (E-0074)

C618.name: wGoldMid
C618.note: middle byte of the gold amount (E-0074)

C619.name: wGoldHi
C619.note: high byte of the gold amount (E-0074)

C49F.name: wBGPaletteBuffer
C49F.note: 8 CGB background palettes (4 RGB555 colours each, 64 bytes) that the fade routines read and write to rBGPD (WriteAllFadedPalettesFloor/Add) (E-0076)

C4DF.name: wOBJPaletteBuffer
C4DF.note: 8 CGB object palettes (64 bytes) that the fade routines write to rOBPD (E-0076)

C572.name: wFadeLevel
C572.note: the 5-bit level the fade routines apply to each colour component (E-0076)

C573.name: wFadeDelay
C573.note: frames between CGB fade steps minus 1, set from wFadeState / 4 by StartPaletteFade_Sub01 and reloaded by StepCGBFade (E-0077)

C574.name: wFadeDelayCounter
C574.note: counts down to the next CGB fade step (StepCGBFade) (E-0077)

C707.name: wKeyList
C707.note: up to 32 4-byte key entries ($FF ends the list; CountKeysOrFull); bytes 1-2 of an entry pick the two words of its name (WriteKeyNameToDE reads from $C708) (E-0090)

C8EF.name: wFollowerRecords
C8EF.note: three 5-byte records for the monsters following the player: direction, X, Y, target X, target Y (SetFollowerTargetsFromLeader, StepFollowersTowardTargets; ScriptSetDirection and ScriptSlideObjectY address the same records) (E-0093)

C920.name: wScriptCommandType
C920.note: the script command being run, 0 = none; indexes ScriptCommandHandlers (minus 1)

C921.name: wScriptParam0
C921.note: first parameter of the current script command

C922.name: wScriptParam1
C922.note: second parameter of the current script command

C923.name: wScriptStep
C923.note: step counter of the current script command

D7FD.name: wScriptInDataBank
D7FD.note: non-zero when the script bytes are read from the bank in wDataBank

D8BF.name: wBattleHP
D8BF.note: current HP of the 8 battle slots as 16-bit words (party in slots 0-2, a foe in slot 4); the first value of the party panels; a defeated foe's word fell from 20 to 0 on the emulator

D8CF.name: wBattleMaxHP
D8CF.note: maximum HP of the 8 battle slots (the foe's word stayed 25 when its current HP fell to 0)

D8DF.name: wBattleMP
D8DF.note: current MP of the 8 battle slots (the values the party panels show as M)

D8EF.name: wBattleMaxMP
D8EF.note: maximum MP of the 8 battle slots, by symmetry with wBattleMaxHP

CFC8.name: wBattlePhase
CFC8.note: battle phase, a 3-entry dispatch in Func_031_40CC: 1 = the fight, 2 = after the fight (victory message, rewards, recruiting); 0 at start (E-0044)

CFC9.name: wBattleStep
CFC9.note: step within the battle phase: in phase 1, 1 = set-up, 2 = command entry (a loop over the party), 3 = executing the chosen actions; in phase 2, 0-5 = the end-of-battle sequence (E-0044)

D8A4.name: wBattleActor
D8A4.note: slot number of the battler whose turn it is: indexes MP arrays and status records in the battle code

D8A5.name: wBattleTarget
D8A5.note: slot number of the battler an action is applied to (ApplyDamageToTarget, DefeatTarget)

DA63.name: wBattleSlotOut
DA63.note: one byte per slot: 1 when the battler is defeated or absent (DefeatTarget sets it; CarryUnlessBattleSlotOutSlotEmpty reads it)

DA1C.name: wBattleActionChoice
DA1C.note: word per slot: byte 0 is the chosen action id, which ChooseActionTarget copies to wBattleActionId; byte 1 is wBattleTargetChoice (E-0061)

DA1D.name: wBattleTargetChoice
DA1D.note: byte 1 of each slot word in wBattleActionChoice: the target slot the per-action target routines write (E-0061)

D0D5.name: wBattlerRecords
D0D5.note: six 78-byte ($4E) battler records for slots 0-2 and 4-6 (BattlerRecordFieldAddress); GetBaseHP reads the HP word at offset $1D (E-0062); the size covers the slot-0 record, the others are wBattlerRecordSlot1-6 (E-0136)

D7F9.name: wMenuInputResult
D7F9.note: result of the bank-$1B/$1D menu cursor routines: $FF confirmed (A), $FE cancelled (B), $FD row moved, $FB page moved, 0 nothing (E-0068)

D7FA.name: wTwoChoiceCursor
D7FA.note: 0 or 1, the selected entry of UpdateTwoChoiceCursor (E-0068)

D006.name: wSpeciesIdLo
D006.note: low byte of the monster id whose species record LoadSpeciesRecord loads (E-0069)

D007.name: wSpeciesIdHi
D007.note: high byte of that monster id (E-0069)

D008.name: wSpeciesRecord
D008.note: 47-byte copy of a species record (LoadSpeciesRecord); byte 0 is the family (E-0069)

D958.name: wBattleMonsterId
D958.note: word per battle slot: the monster id (the species-record and monster-name number; CopyMonsterNameOfDisplaySlotToDE, GetSlotSpeciesFamily) (E-0069)

C924.name: wMessageIndex
C924.note: string index of the message RunMessageBox shows (low byte of the message word) (E-0079)

C925.name: wMessageGroup
C925.note: message word high byte: bits 0-5 select the message group (ShowMessageHL), bit 7 skips opening the window, bit 6 skips closing it (E-0079)

C926.name: wMessageState
C926.note: RunMessageBox state: 0-3 while a message runs, $FF when idle; StartMessageA sets 0 (E-0079)

C92C.name: wStepArrived
C92C.note: 1 when the last StepObjectTowardCoord or StepPlayer*TowardWC928 step reached the target coordinate in wC928, else 0 (E-0071)

DAAC.name: wQueuedActionId
DAAC.note: queued action id. One writer read so far stores $FF when a target's pending bit 4 (wD814 + 9 * target) is consumed (ResolveStepDamageMessage_Sub04_Case04); banks $19 and $A0 also write it and are not read yet; read by QueuedActionMatches (E-0049)

D80C.name: wBattleStatus
D80C.note: 9-byte status record per slot (AddAx9ToHL), cleared when the battler is defeated

DAC4.name: wBattleStatResultLo
DAC4.note: low byte of the 16-bit result of the GetBase* routines (wDAC5 is the high byte)

D872.name: wBattleDamageLo
D872.note: low byte of the damage ApplyDamageToTarget subtracts (wD873 is the high byte)

DAC5.name: wBattleStatResultHi
DAC5.note: high byte of the 16-bit result of the GetBase* routines

CFCA.name: wBattleSubPhase
CFCA.note: index within the battle step: during step 3 of phase 1 it counts the actions being executed (0, 1, 2, ...); during command entry it alternates 1 and 2 (E-0044)

CFCB.name: wBattleResolveStep
CFCB.note: step of RunBattleResolveStep (16 cases, 0-15) for the action wBattleSubPhase is executing; ApplyDamageToTarget advances or rewinds it (E-0044)

CFCC.name: wBattleSubStep
CFCC.note: nested step used by Func_032_5EAB (10 cases) and cleared by ApplyDamageToTarget

CFCD.name: wBattleSubStep2
CFCD.note: nested step used by Func_032_5A3A (3 cases)

D8FF.name: wBattleATK
D8FF.note: attack of the 8 battle slots: ComputeBasicDamage reads the actor's word from it and the defence array for the target; 8 words, party in slots 0-2

D90F.name: wBattleDEF
D90F.note: defence of the 8 battle slots; RecomputeBattler (Func_032_5BE8) fills it from GetBaseDEF

D91F.name: wBattleAGL
D91F.note: agility of the 8 battle slots; Func_032_5BE8 fills it from GetBaseAGL

D92F.name: wBattleINT
D92F.note: intelligence of the 8 battle slots, the array after wBattleAGL (assumed)

D8A6.name: wBattleActionId
D8A6.note: id of the action being resolved; the resolve steps compare it with fixed values ($13-$15, $79, $91, $D6, $D7, $DC), some above the SkillTable range of 175, so it is an action number rather than a skill index

FF8A.name: hPlayerSpriteVariant
FF8A.note: first byte of the 14 HRAM bytes saved with the game (SaveGameToSRAMWithChecksum); LoadPlayerSpriteGraphics sets it to 0 or 1 by story flag 0 and picks the player graphics with it

FF8B.name: hPlayerSpriteMode
FF8B.note: sprite mode 0-2 chosen from story flags $19F, $25, 2 and bit 3 of hPlayerStateFlags (LoadPlayerAndFollowerSpriteGraphics); AdvancePlayerAnimCounterAndRunPlayerSpriteMode dispatches on it

FF8C.name: hPlayerStateFlags
FF8C.note: player state bits: bit 0 = a step is in progress, bit 2 = moving, bit 1 freezes the animation counter, bits 3, 5, 6, 7 are field-state flags tested before moving, menus and warps

FF8D.name: hFieldDrawFlags
FF8D.note: field draw flags: InitFieldScreen sets $0F; routines set and clear bits 1-3 around record-list redraws; saved and restored with the sprite state (wD7BA)

FF93.name: hPlayerSpriteOverride
FF93.note: bit 7 set: the player uses the graphics stream in hPlayerSpriteStream and a countdown (hPlayerSpriteTimer) runs; set by script commands $A0/$A1

FF94.name: hPlayerSpriteStreamLo
FF94.note: low byte of the compressed stream used for the player graphics when bit 7 of hPlayerSpriteOverride is set

FF96.name: hPlayerSpriteTimerLo
FF96.note: low byte of a countdown decremented each field update while the sprite override is on; when it goes negative, talk event $0A is dispatched (UpdatePlayerMovement_Sub01_Sub03)

FF99.name: hPlayerAnimCounter
FF99.note: animation counter: +1 per field frame (+3 more while moving) unless bit 1 of hPlayerStateFlags is set

FF9A.name: hPlayerTurnDelay
FF9A.note: frames to wait after turning in place (set to 4) before the player can step (UpdatePlayerMovement)

FF9B.name: hPlayerStepDXLo
FF9B.note: low byte of the 16-bit horizontal step delta per frame (+$10, -$10, or screen-scroll values) set when a step starts

FF9C.name: hPlayerStepDXHi
FF9C.note: high byte of the horizontal step delta

FF9D.name: hPlayerStepDYLo
FF9D.note: low byte of the 16-bit vertical step delta (for example $FF80 when scrolling up a screen)

FF9E.name: hPlayerStepDYHi
FF9E.note: high byte of the vertical step delta

FF9F.name: hWindowX
FF9F.note: copied to rWX by CopyScrollToHardware; 7 in the field (InitFieldScreen)

FFA0.name: hWindowY
FFA0.note: copied to rWY by CopyScrollToHardware; $80 (off screen) in the field

FFB3.name: hMetaSpriteYLo
FFB3.note: metasprite builder: low byte of origin Y plus the scroll offset, added to each entry's Y

FFB4.name: hMetaSpriteYHi
FFB4.note: metasprite builder: high byte of that Y, used to drop entries outside the screen

FFB5.name: hMetaSpriteXLo
FFB5.note: metasprite builder: low byte of origin X plus the scroll offset

FFB6.name: hMetaSpriteXHi
FFB6.note: metasprite builder: high byte of that X

FFB7.name: hMetaSpriteXFlipLo
FFB7.note: metasprite builder: X minus 8, low byte, used for horizontally flipped sets

FFB8.name: hMetaSpriteXFlipHi
FFB8.note: metasprite builder: high byte of X minus 8

FFB9.name: hSpriteWindowClipMode
FFB9.note: non-zero makes the metasprite builders take the clipping path; set to 2 or 3 while a text window or menu is open and 0 when it closes

FFBA.name: hSpriteHideTile
FFBA.note: BG tile id compared with the tile under a sprite point (BGTileUnderPointIsHFFBA_*); sprite parts over this tile are hidden; usually $80

FFBF.name: hDecompressRunCount
FFBF.note: decompressor: count of the current run or copy (DecompressToRAM / DecompressToVRAM)

FFC0.name: hDecompressRunByte
FFC0.note: decompressor: byte being repeated or the current control byte

FFC5.name: hVRAMByteTemp
FFC5.note: byte held while waiting for VRAM access (DecompressToVRAM, CopyRectToBGMapWrapped_1C)

FFC6.name: hTemp0
FFC6.note: general argument and result byte: SRAM record loads return here, field commands and many helpers take their argument here (used in 54 bank files)

FFC7.name: hTemp1
FFC7.note: general argument/result byte after hTemp0 (high byte of word results)

FFC8.name: hTemp2
FFC8.note: general argument/result byte (third byte of 24-bit and BCD results)

FFCA.name: hTemp4
FFCA.note: general argument/result byte (also a VRAM destination low byte for DecompressGraphicsTemp0ToTemp4)

FFCB.name: hTemp5
FFCB.note: general argument/result byte (destination high byte for DecompressGraphicsTemp0ToTemp4)

FFD1.name: hVRAMWriteByte
FFD1.note: A saved by WriteVRAMByte / WriteVRAMByteInc while waiting for VRAM access

FFDA.name: hSndChanFlags
FFDA.note: sound channel copy (the 32-byte slot is copied to $FFD8): low 2 bits = hardware channel, high nibble set by track command $A3

FFDE.name: hSndDutyAndTempo
FFDE.note: sound channel copy: bits 6-7 = duty (command $A2 / track header), low nibble = tempo step added to hSndTickAccum each tick

FFDF.name: hSndTickAccum
FFDF.note: sound channel copy: tick accumulator; the channel advances when it passes 16

FFE0.name: hSndEnvelope
FFE0.note: sound channel copy: volume envelope written to NRx2 (command $A0, track header)

FFE1.name: hSndWaitTicks
FFE1.note: sound channel copy: ticks left before the next event (set by notes and command $A7)

FFE2.name: hSndSweepOrWave
FFE2.note: sound channel copy: NR10 sweep value for channel 1, wave index for channel 3 (command $A1)

FFE3.name: hSndChanByteE3
FFE3.note: sound channel copy: cleared when a track starts; no other use found

FFE4.name: hSndBranchIndex
FFE4.note: sound channel copy: index used by command $A9 (set, increment, decrement, or jump through a table by it)

FFE5.name: hSndVibratoDepth
FFE5.note: sound channel copy: depth nibble from commands $Cx

FFE6.name: hSndVibratoDelay
FFE6.note: sound channel copy: delay value from commands $Cx (and $A2 on channel 3)

FFE7.name: hSndVibratoCounter
FFE7.note: sound channel copy: counts up to hSndVibratoDelay after each note

FFE8.name: hSndPitchSlide
FFE8.note: sound channel copy: signed pitch slide per step (commands $Dx/$Ex)

FFE9.name: hSndPitchSlideTime
FFE9.note: sound channel copy: slide interval reload

FFEA.name: hSndPitchSlideCounter
FFEA.note: sound channel copy: slide interval counter

FFEB.name: hSndFreqLo
FFEB.note: sound channel copy: frequency low byte written to NRx3

FFEC.name: hSndFreqHi
FFEC.note: sound channel copy: frequency high byte (with the trigger bit) written to NRx4

FFED.name: hSndEnvelopeReload
FFED.note: sound channel copy: high nibble = envelope restored when the envelope timer expires (command $AA)

FFEE.name: hSndPanning
FFEE.note: sound channel copy: panning bits merged into NR51 for this channel (command $A5)

FFEF.name: hSndNoteLength
FFEF.note: sound channel copy: note length reload (command $A3, low nibble x 2)

FFF0.name: hSndNoteTimer
FFF0.note: sound channel copy: note length counter

FFF1.name: hSndA8Param
FFF1.note: sound channel copy: parameter of command $A8 (its high nibble picks the wave table set)

FFF3.name: hSndEnvFlags
FFF3.note: sound channel copy: envelope timer flags and reload (command $AA)

FFF4.name: hSndLoopCount
FFF4.note: sound channel copy: repeat counter of command $AC

FFF5.name: hSndReturnPosLo
FFF5.note: sound channel copy: track position to return to (command $AD), low byte

FFF6.name: hSndReturnPosHi
FFF6.note: sound channel copy: return position, high byte

C000.name: wShadowOAM

D895.name: wActionQueue
D895.note: 8-byte queue of slots waiting to act ($FF = empty; RemoveCFromActionQueue)

D89F.name: wBattleMeter
D89F.note: 16-bit battle meter: each action adds an amount, capped at 1800 (AddHLToBattleMeterCappedAt1800, SubtractHLFromBattleMeterFloored)

D8A1.name: wBattleInitA1
D8A1.note: set by GameMode4_Init_Sub01, read at the battle end

D8A7.name: wSlotDamageFlags
D8A7.note: per-slot flags: bit 0 multiplies some damage (MultiplyDamageBy50IfSlotDamageFlagsBit0, AttackDamageTimes1_5IfSlotDamageFlagsBit0)

D8AF.name: wSlotNameSuffix
D8AF.note: per-slot byte: bit 0 picks the letter appended to a repeated monster name (CopyBattleMonsterNameWithLetterSuffix)

D8B7.name: wBattleLevel
D8B7.note: level of each battle slot (DrawSlotLevel_BankA0, DrainTargetMPAmount)

D960.name: wBattlePictureIds
D960.note: three monster ids whose pictures the battle intro shows (LoadBattleMonsterPictureAttributes, BattlePhase0_Step2)

D988.name: wBattleSkillsPrefix
D988.note: byte before wBattleSkills, indexed by 16 * slot

D989.name: wBattleSkills
D989.note: skills of the 8 battle slots, 16 bytes each (8 skill numbers at even offsets; SlotHasSkillWithFlagD)

DA3C.name: wAIChoiceWeights
DA3C.note: three AI choice weights sorted by SortThreeAIWeightsRandomTies

DA3F.name: wAIChoiceOrder
DA3F.note: choice indexes that follow the weights when sorted

DA43.name: wSlotTactic
DA43.note: per-slot battle tactic, low 2 bits; 3 = manual command (GetActorSlotTacticLow2, SetSlotTacticAndSlotLastTacticForCommandMonster)

DA4B.name: wSlotLastTactic
DA4B.note: last tactic other than 3 for each slot

DA53.name: wSlotAIMode
DA53.note: per-slot AI mode (SetSlotAIModeFromINT; values below 3 skip some checks)

DA5B.name: wSlotMarks
DA5B.note: per-slot mark set for present slots (SetSlotMarksForPresentSlots, SetTargetSlotMarksTo3)

DA6B.name: wBattleExpAward
DA6B.note: 24-bit EXP award at the battle end (DivideBattleExpAwardByModeFactor, AddExpToRecordCCapped); the AI scoring loop keeps its routine table pointer in the first two bytes

DA6E.name: wAISkillScore
DA6E.note: AI score word of the skill being scored (ResetAISkillScore, AddBCToAISkillScore)

DA70.name: wAISkillScore2
DA70.note: second AI score word ($FFFF after reset; AddBCToAISkillScore2)

DA72.name: wSlotResistances
DA72.note: 8 seven-byte resistance records, one per slot (GetTargetSlotResistancesByte0-6; 2-bit levels)

DAAA.name: wEffectActive
DAAA.note: non-zero while the battle effect animation runs

DAAB.name: wDisplaySlot
DAAB.note: slot whose name or picture is shown (CopyMonsterNameOfDisplaySlotToDE, LoadBattleMonsterPictureAndTitle)

DAAE.name: wSpecialSlotMonsters
DAAE.note: monster id words used for slots 3 and 7 (GetBaseHP, TatsuCall, Transform)

DAB2.name: wResolveFlagB2
DAB2.note: resolve flag (bit 0 skips the action text in RunBattleStep4_Case00_Sub01_Case02)

DAB7.name: wEffectSpriteAttrXor
DAB7.note: attribute XOR of the effect sprite (DrawEffectSpriteAtWD804_*)

DAB9.name: wEffectTargetMode
DAB9.note: effect target mode (3 moves the sprite; SetEffectSpriteXForTargets)

DABD.name: wFollowUpAction
DABD.note: non-zero while a follow-up action runs (ResolveStepBegin, ResolveStepCallEffect82)

DABE.name: wDefeatStep
DABE.note: defeat sequence step + 1 (RunDefeatStepMinus1Step; set by DefeatTarget)

DAC0.name: wResolveMsgFlags
DAC0.note: message flags of the resolving action: bit 4 picks the actor or target side (ResolveStepDamageMessage)

DAC2.name: wResolveMsgActor
DAC2.note: message id for the actor side

DAC3.name: wResolveMsgTarget
DAC3.note: message id for the target side

DAC9.name: wSavedActorTarget
DAC9.note: actor and target saved by RunBattleStep4_Case00_Sub01_Case00

DAD4.name: wSlotNameBytes
DAD4.note: three bytes set at battle start, checked by CopySlotNameToHL

DAD8.name: wSideControl
DAD8.note: per-slot control byte: bit 7 set = AI controlled (ChooseTargetForActor, AIChooseActionResolveStep)

DAF1.name: wEffectFrameCounter
DAF1.note: frame counter for the every-fifth-frame effect step

DAFA.name: wHealFlags
DAFA.note: bytes indexed per slot by HealTargetHP and LoveRain

DC20.name: wSoundChannel1
DC20.note: sound channel slot 1 (6 slots of $20 bytes from wSoundChannelSlots)

DD08.name: wSoundSkipMaskA
DD08.note: ANDed with wSoundSkipMaskB; non-zero makes ReturnTwiceIfSoundSkipMaskAAndSoundSkipMaskB skip the caller

DD0C.name: wSoundTickByte0C
DD0C.note: set by SoundTick, read by SoundNextEvent

DD0D.name: wSoundRegBase
DD0D.note: register base ($FF00 offset) of the channel being processed (WriteChannelRegisterC)

DD19.name: wSoundInitByte19
DD19.note: set by InitSoundHardware, read by SoundTick

A000.name: sRecords
A000.note: SRAM bank 0: the monster records, $A5 bytes each from here (SRAMRecordAddress, LoadSRAMRecordByte); in SRAM bank 1 the extra record $1D sits here (RecordAddressWithBank1Slot1D)

A0A5.name: sRecord1
A0A5.note: second $A5-byte record (DeleteSRAMRecordAndCompact moves the records from here down)

A06F.name: sBank1Records
A06F.note: SRAM bank 1: compact $6F-byte records (SRAMBank1RecordAddress); the bank-1 checksum covers $29A * 10 bytes from here

AD71.name: sRecordBackup
AD71.note: SRAM bank 1: backup of the compact records and the bank-1 record (BackupRecordsToSRAMBank1, RestoreRecordsFromSRAMBank1Backup)

B356.name: sCompactRecords
B356.note: SRAM bank 0: 29 compact $6F-byte records after the 30 full records (RecordAddressWithBank1Slot1D, CountFlaggedSRAMRecords)

BA73.name: sBank1Checksum
BA73.note: SRAM bank 1: complement of the record sum plus $4321 (ComputeSRAMBank1RecordChecksum, VerifySaveBank1Checksum)

BB00.name: sSaveSignature
BB00.note: SRAM bank 1: $55 when a save exists (CheckSaveData)

BB01.name: sSaveData
BB01.note: SRAM bank 1: the saved blocks in order: hFF8A ($0E bytes), wPlayerName block ($291), wStoryFlags ($6B), wKeyWorldSlot block ($B5) (SaveGameToSRAMWithChecksum)

BD30.name: sSavedPlayTime
BD30.note: saved play time from wPlayFrames (5 bytes)

BE0D.name: sSavedMapType
BE0D.note: saved wMapType (the title screen shows a key name for special maps)

BEC0.name: sSavedCE9BBlock
BEC0.note: SRAM bank 1: copy of the $D8-byte block at wGM2TimerFrames (SaveGM2TimerFramesBlockToSRAMBank1)

BF98.name: sSaveChecksumLo
BF98.note: SRAM bank 1: low byte of the saved blocks sum + $9753

C53F.name: wPlayerNameText
C53F.note: the player name copied with a $F0 terminator for text output (StepStringDisplayUntilDone_Sub01_Sub02_Case16)

C570.note: second DMG palette byte of the fade

C571.note: third DMG palette byte of the fade

CCCD.name: wNameBufUnknown
CCCD.note: name buffer picked when a name starts with the $98 placeholder (PickNameBufferForFirstByte)

CECF.name: wTopSpeciesName
CECF.note: name of the picked species, copied from wNameGlyphBuf (GameMode5_Update_Case07_Sub01_Sub04)

CEDC.name: wTopSpeciesByteDC
CEDC.note: byte passed as wArg2 with the picked species

D00F.name: wSpeciesExpCurve
D00F.note: species record byte 7: the ExpTable row (EXP curve) of the species (LoadTable4E60EntryForWC991ToWC9DE)
